decision: Dropped exact duplicate rows, keeping the first copy.
reason: A registry row repeated in every column is the same patient entered twice, so keeping one copy makes patient_id a unique key.

issue: gender spellings that are not a code
decision: Stripped and lowercased gender, mapped each spelling to F, M, or X, and stored it as a category.
reason: Spellings such as woman, MALE, M with a trailing space, and non-binary name the same three codes, while empty and unknown entries were never recorded and become missing.

decision: Uppercased site_code and removed every hyphen and space.
reason: Entries such as n-01 or S 02 refer to N01 and S02, and the site join needs the exact code to match sites.csv.

decision: Replaced 9999 with a missing value and stored birth_year as Int64.
reason: The data dictionary says 9999 means not recorded, so keeping it as a year would distort the minimum, maximum, and any age.

issue: weight column named wt_kg in visits_south.csv
decision: Renamed wt_kg to weight_kg in a copy of the south table before stacking.
reason: Both offices record the same weight in kg, and concat aligns columns by name, so a different name would split weight into two half-empty columns.

issue: sbp sentinel 999 and readings outside 70 through 250
decision: Set 999 and every reading below 70 or above 250 mmHg to missing, keeping 70 and 250, and stored sbp_mmhg as Int64.
reason: 999 means not measured and readings outside 70 through 250 are not plausible systolic pressures, while the planted 70 and 250 values sit on the inclusive range.

issue: impossible and loosely written visit dates
decision: Kept visit_date only when the text is exact YYYY-MM-DD for a real calendar date, and set the rest to missing.
reason: Values like 2026/04/27, 2026-3-06, or a day that does not exist on the calendar cannot be trusted as written, so guessing a date would invent data.

decision: Mapped the visit labels, removed exact repeats, then kept the later reading of each remaining pair by visit_time.
reason: After mapping, labels such as wk12 and week12 name the same visit, and a second reading at a later time is a recheck that should replace the first.

decision: Kept only rows whose record_status is current, with site_code and site_name.
reason: N01 and S02 each have a retired and a current record, and keeping both would duplicate every patient row in the site join.
